skill.name: debugging
skill.description: Guides agents through a four-phase debugging process: reproduce the issue, find root cause, compare patterns, test one hypothesis, and verify the fix.
skill.summary: Structured debugging process for root cause investigation before fixes.
skill.author: ArcadeAI

security_audit.summary: The static backtick and reconnaissance alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, read-only diagnostic examples, and normal debugging checklist text. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found, but the skill grants broad tool access with allowed-tools '*'.

remediation.suggestion: Replace allowed-tools '*' with the minimum tools needed for reading files, running tests, and read-only git inspection.
Add guidance to redact secrets, tokens, customer data, and production queries before logging boundary values.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Tool Permission
semantic_findings.description: The skill declares allowed-tools '*', which grants every available tool when the skill is active. A debugging workflow should use scoped permissions because broad access increases the impact of prompt injection or accidental destructive actions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The frontmatter explicitly grants all tools. This is a real configuration risk, although the skill text itself does not show malicious intent.

content.user_title: Debug Failures With Root Cause Discipline
content.value_statement: Bug fixes often fail when agents patch symptoms before understanding causes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured investigation and verification.
actual_capabilities: Requires root cause investigation before any fix is proposed.
Prompts complete reading of errors, stack traces, warnings, and recent code changes.
Structures reproduction checks, data-flow tracing, and comparison with working examples.
Guides single-hypothesis testing with one minimal change at a time.
Requires a failing test and verification against existing tests before completion.
limitations: It is a process guide, not an automated debugger.
It cannot diagnose issues without errors, logs, tests, or reproducible steps.
It may slow small fixes because it requires investigation before implementation.
Its broad tool permission should be narrowed before automatic installation.

use_cases.title: Reproduce Test Failures
use_cases.description: Use the framework to collect full errors, reproduce the failure, and verify the fix with focused tests.

use_cases.title: Trace Service Bugs
use_cases.description: Follow data across API, service, and database layers to find where bad input or state appears.

use_cases.title: Recover From Failed Fixes
use_cases.description: Stop repeated patching, review each failed attempt, and decide whether the design needs a deeper change.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Debugging Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the debugging skill to investigate this error. Read the full error, identify missing information, and do not propose a fix until you have a root cause.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new bug or test failure

prompt_templates.title: Reproduce and Compare
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the debugging skill on this failing behavior. Help me reproduce it consistently, then compare the broken path with similar working code.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Multi-Layer Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the debugging skill to trace this API-to-service-to-database failure. Add minimal boundary observations, identify where data changes, and state one hypothesis.

prompt_templates.title: Review Failed Fix Attempts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the debugging skill after these failed fixes. Reassess the architecture, explain why each fix failed, and recommend whether to refactor or continue.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced recovery after repeated unsuccessful fixes

output_examples.input: A test fails only in CI after a dependency update.
output: The response requests the full CI error and dependency change list.
It separates reproduction facts from hypotheses.
It proposes one minimal test to confirm the likely dependency behavior.

output_examples.input: An API returns empty results even though the database has records.
output: The response traces the request through API, service, and database boundaries.
It identifies where the data first becomes empty.
It recommends fixing the source layer and verifying existing tests.

output_examples.input: Two previous fixes did not resolve a flaky issue.
output: The response reviews what each failed fix proved.
It forms a new root cause hypothesis from the failed attempts.
It advises stopping for architecture review if another fix fails.

best_practices: Provide full errors, logs, recent changes, and exact reproduction steps.
Let the skill complete investigation before asking for implementation.
Run one test or observation at a time so results remain attributable.
anti_patterns: Ask for a quick fix before the root cause is known.
Bundle multiple unrelated fixes into one debugging attempt.
Ignore failed fix history when the same issue keeps returning.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a debugging process. Actual tool use depends on the host agent and configured permissions.

faq.question: Which agents can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it fix production incidents?
faq.answer: It can guide incident debugging, but users must provide logs, symptoms, and safe operational boundaries.

faq.question: Does it replace tests?
faq.answer: No. It asks for a failing test before the fix and verification after the fix.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it for bugs, failing tests, unexpected behavior, performance issues, or repeated failed fixes.

faq.question: What security concern exists?
faq.answer: The skill currently grants all tools in its frontmatter. Marketplace operators should require narrower permissions.
